title: Redirect SubD grid flow with a continuous local perimeter ring

defect: rounded corner that should read sharper

preconditions: the reference requires a more controlled perimeter radius or highlight
interior grid flow currently runs directly into that perimeter
the affected region can accept a continuous quad ring without creating concave or overlapping faces
required_observations: base wire topology around the complete boundary
fixed-frame MatCap or reflective highlight before and after
localized surface diagnostics interpreted as candidates only
action_policy: Inset or author one continuous local ring that follows the boundary so interior flow terminates against the ring instead of diverging into the edge.
Keep the ring width tied to the required physical radius; do not add dense global support for one local boundary.
Reject the ring when it only increases density, creates concentrated corner artifacts, or contradicts a deliberately soft reference edge.
expected_effects: sharper but still continuous SubD boundary
recovery: remove or widen the support ring
use crease when the edge requires sharpness without a physical support radius

sources.description: Ryuu - Blender Bros demonstrates an inset perimeter loop to redirect flow and clean a boundary highlight.

experiments.limitations: One sloped rectangular boundary. The correction costs three times the evaluated faces and has not yet transferred to a different boundary family.

version_scope: Blender 5.2 LTS reproduction; source tutorial used Blender 3.6
status_note: One tutorial reproduction supports the rule; different-geometry transfer and a complete advanced asset are still required.
